delete.summary: Delete a course and all of its data (grades, files, schedule).
delete.description: Irreversible. Use only when the user clearly asks to delete the course.

get.summary: Get one course with its terms, credits, instructors and resolved color.
get.description: Use when you need the details of a course whose id you know.

patch.summary: Change a course's code, title, alias, credits, color, instructors or other fields.
patch.description:
Partial update: only the fields that are sent change. To move a course to other
terms or make it year-long, use academics.course.set_terms.

put.description: Courses not listed keep their default order after the listed ones.

put.description:
Replaces the course's terms. They must belong to its Program and be next to each
other in time.

get.summary: List the user's Programs (degrees) with their term and course counts.
get.description:
Use to find the Program ids of the user, e.g. before listing terms or courses
when no Program is given. Most users have exactly one Program.

post.summary: Create a Program (a degree or study plan).
post.description:
Use only when the user explicitly wants a new, separate Program, e.g. a second
degree. Do not use to add a term or a course; use academics.term.create or
academics.course.create.

delete.summary: Delete a Program with all of its terms, courses and their data.
delete.description:
Irreversible. Use only when the user clearly asks to delete the whole Program.
To remove one term or course use academics.term.delete or academics.course.delete.

get.summary: Get one Program: name, school, time zone, credit defaults and subject colors.
get.description: Use when you need a Program's details such as its time zone or credit goal.

patch.summary: Change a Program's name, school, time zone or credit settings.
patch.description: Partial update: only the fields that are sent change.

put.summary: Set the color of a subject code (e.g. all 'APS' courses) in a Program.
put.description:
Use when the user wants every course of a subject in another color. To color a
single course differently, use academics.course.update with `color`.

get.summary: Week numbers of a term: each week's dates, number or break, and today's week.
get.description:
Use to translate between dates and week numbers ("week 6", "reading week"),
e.g. to resolve "the Friday of week 3". Week 1 is the week the term starts in.

post.summary: Create a term, optionally with its courses, in one step.
post.description:
Use when the user starts a new semester. Check academics.term.list first so the
term does not exist already. `courses` creates courses in the new term; `continue_course_ids`
extends year-long courses of the previous term into it.

get.summary: List the terms (semesters) of a Program in chronological order.

Use to find a term id, or which term is current (`is_current`), before creating
courses or answering questions about a semester.

delete.summary: Delete a term and the courses that are only in it.
delete.description:
Irreversible. Year-long courses that also run in other terms are kept and only
lose this term. Show academics.term.delete_preview to the user first.

get.summary: Get one term with its dates and breaks.
get.description: Use when you need a term's dates, reading weeks or holidays.

patch.summary: Change a term's name, dates, breaks or week numbering.
patch.description:
Partial update. `breaks` replaces the whole list; keep the ids of breaks that
stay. Fails with academics.course_terms_not_adjacent when new dates would separate the terms of
a year-long course.

get.summary: What deleting a term would remove: its own courses vs. year-long courses kept.
get.description: Use before academics.term.delete to tell the user what will be deleted.

calendar.occurrences. Times are UTC; read them in the returned `timezone`.

post.summary: Add an assessment (quiz, exam, assignment...) to a course gradebook.
post.description:
Use when the user adds a graded item. Give the deadline as `due_date` (and
`due_time` if known) in the Program's time zone. Do not use to record a score on an existing
assessment; use grading.assessment.update.

get.summary: List a course's assessments with deadline, weight and score.
get.description:
Use to see what is graded, still pending or overdue in a course. To locate one
assessment the user named in words ("Lab 3", "the midterm"), prefer grading.assessment.find.

parameters.name: status

schema.description: graded, pending (no score yet) or overdue (pending, past due)
schema.title: Status

parameters.description: graded, pending (no score yet) or overdue (pending, past due)

schema.title: Fields

post.summary: Add several assessments at once (imports from a syllabus or an LMS).
post.description:
Items that carry `source_kind` and `source_ref` are skipped when the course
already has an assessment from the same source, so repeating an import creates no duplicates.

delete.summary: Delete an assessment from a gradebook.
delete.description: Irreversible. To ignore an assessment in the grade, set `dropped` instead.

patch.summary: Change an assessment, mainly to record its score.
patch.description:
Record a score with `score_percentage` (82), or `points_earned` with
`points_possible` (18 of 20). Send null to clear the score again. Also changes title, category,
deadline, weight, `dropped` (ignore it in every calculation) and note. Only the fields that are sent
change.

put.summary: Set the order of a course's assessments.
put.description: Assessments not listed keep their order after the listed ones.

post.summary: Add an assessment category (e.g. 'Midterm') to a course's gradebook.
post.description: Use when the syllabus has a kind of assessment the built-in categories lack.

delete.summary: Delete an assessment category; its assessments become uncategorised.
delete.description: Irreversible, but no assessment is deleted. Prefer archiving.

patch.summary: Rename, recolor or archive an assessment category.
patch.description: Partial update. Archived categories keep their assessments but leave the pickers.

put.summary: Set the display order of a course's assessment categories.
put.description: Categories not listed keep their order after the listed ones.

patch.summary: Change how a course is graded: official final grade, target, pass/fail, forecast.
patch.description:
Use to enter the official final grade (`final_override_percentage`, which wins
over the calculated one; null clears it), set the target in grade points, switch a course to
pass/fail, or enter a final grade for a course without a gradebook (`manual_percentage` with
`gradebook_enabled: false`). To record the score of one assessment use
grading.assessment.update.

get.summary: The grade, grade points and status of every course in a Program.
get.description: Use to compare courses or list which are finished, in progress or pass/fail.

parameters.name: include_in_progress

schema.title: Include In Progress

get.summary: A course's gradebook: categories, assessments, and every calculated figure.
get.description:
Use to answer questions about a course's grade: the current average, the final
grade, the forecast, or what the remaining assessments must average to reach a target grade
(`summary.required_average`). The summary figures are null while the weights do not add up to
100 (`summary.weight_gap` says how much is missing). Never calculate grades yourself.

get.summary: Get a Program's grading scale: percentage ranges → grade points and letters.
get.description:
Use to convert a percentage to grade points or a letter, or to read the Program's
grading defaults (how year-long courses count, default categories, hidden GPA).

put.summary: Change a Program's grading scale or grading defaults.
put.description:
Partial update: only the fields that are sent change. `bands` replaces the whole
table; the ranges must not overlap and must reach from 0 to 100, with points of at most
`max_points`. Every GPA of the Program is recalculated from the new scale.

get.summary: List the built-in grading scales (UofT 4.0, US 4.0, China 100-point, custom).
get.description: Use to offer ready-made scales; apply one with grading.scale.update.

post.summary: What-if: the course figures if ungraded assessments scored the given marks.
post.description:
Use to answer "what if I get 80 on the final". Nothing is saved: never change
real scores to simulate. Fails with grading.weights_not_100 while the weights do not add up.

post.summary: What-if for a term: the term GPA if unfinished courses ended with given marks.
post.description:
Pass assumed final percentages per unfinished course in `scores`; with
`target_gpa` the result says whether it is reachable and what average the other unfinished courses
need. Nothing is saved.

post.summary: Suggest a score for every ungraded assessment that reaches the target grade.
post.description:
Scores follow the student's results so far in each category and land exactly on
the target. Used to auto-fill a what-if plan. Fails with grading.weights_not_100 while the
weights do not add up.

get.summary: Cumulative GPA, earned credits, progress to graduation and GPA per term.
get.description:
Use for "what is my overall GPA" or "how many credits do I have left". Every
course counts once, a year-long one in the term the Program's setting names.

post.summary: Check or uncheck a habit for a day (today or the past 7 days).
post.description:
Use when the user says they did a habit ("check in my reading habit"). Find the
instance_id with layouts.board.get (the habit card of the course, term, Program or today board).
Calling it on a day that is already checked removes the check-in, so read habit.checkins.list
first when the user only wants it checked. Days older than 7 days or in the future are refused.

get.summary: List the checked days of a habit within a date range.
get.description:

Program's time zone.

get.summary: Current streak, longest streak and total check-ins of a habit.
get.description:
Use to answer how long the user's streak is or how often they did a habit. For a
weekly goal the streaks count weeks that reached the weekly target; a streak stays alive while
the running day (or week) is still open. Also returns today's date in the Program's time zone.

post.summary: Add a weekly (or biweekly) class section to a course in one of its terms.
post.description:

schedule.conflicts afterwards and mention any overlap. For a single extra session (exam, make-up
class) use schedule.event.create instead.

get.summary: List a course's weekly class sections, with their cancelled or moved dates.
get.description:
Use to see when a course meets each week, or to find the meeting id before
changing or cancelling one class. Optionally only one term of a year-long course.

post.summary: Add several class sections to a course at once (imports).
post.description:
Used by importers. An item with the same source_kind and source_ref as an
existing meeting of the course updates it instead of adding a duplicate.

delete.summary: Delete a class section with all its dates.
delete.description:
Removes the section entirely. To cancel one class use
schedule.exception.upsert with kind 'cancelled'; to hide a section the user does not attend use
schedule.meeting.set_enabled.

patch.summary: Change a class section for the whole term (time, room, weeks, ...).
patch.description:
Changes every week. To change or cancel a single date use
schedule.exception.upsert instead.

put.summary: Show or hide class sections of a course, e.g. keep only the user's tutorial.
put.description: Disabled sections stay in the course but are left out of the calendar.

get.summary: Get the user's personal preferences.
get.description:
Use when you need the user's language, clock format (12h/24h) or first day of
the week, for example to format a time or date in the way the user expects.
Do not use to read per-module settings such as the calendar default view;
use settings.values.get.

patch.summary: Change personal preferences (language, theme, accent, clock, week start).
patch.description: Partial update: only the fields that are sent change. Not for agents.

get.summary: List every settings namespace with its fields.
get.description:
Use before changing a module setting to find the namespace, the field names,
their allowed values and the levels (account, program, term, course) where they can be set.
Do not use to read current values; use settings.values.get.

post.summary: Read several UI state entries at once.
post.description:
Reads interface state (sort orders, collapsed panels) by key or key prefix.
Not available to agents.

put.description: Stores interface state under a key. Not available to agents.

get.summary: Get the effective settings of a module or plugin at a scope.
get.description:
Use when the user asks how a module is configured, e.g. the default calendar
view. Returns the effective value of every field and the level it is inherited from
(default, account, program, term or course).
Do not use for personal preferences such as language or theme; use settings.preferences.get.

open in month view. Only the given fields are set at that level; deeper levels still override them.
Look up namespace and field names with settings.schemas.list first.
Do not use to change language, theme or other personal preferences.

delete.summary: Remove one setting at a scope level so it is inherited again.
delete.description:
Restores a field to the value of the level above (or the default).
Not available to agents.

Use when the user asks to jot something down in a note ("note the midterm scope
in this course's sticky"). It replaces the whole text, so call sticky.note.list first and send
the old text with the new lines added. At most 10 000 characters.
